remediation_steps.title: Assess Redis Memory Utilization and Apply Temporary Write Freeze
remediation_steps.description: Collect real‑time Redis metrics, confirm >98% memory usage, and enable a write‑freeze to prevent further data ingestion while remediation proceeds.
commands: kubectl exec -n cache $(kubectl get pod -n cache -l app=redis-primary -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- redis-cli INFO memory
kubectl exec -n cache $(kubectl get pod -n cache -l app=redis-primary -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
kubectl exec -n cache $(kubectl get pod -n cache -l app=redis-primary -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- redis-cli CONFIG SET stop-writes-on-bgsave-error yes
kubectl exec -n cache $(kubectl get pod -n cache -l app=redis-primary -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- redis-cli CONFIG SET stop-writes-on-replication-failure yes
verification: Write‑freeze flag is active (no new writes accepted)

remediation_steps.description: Promote the healthy read‑replica to primary, then increase the Redis pod memory limit to alleviate exhaustion.

verification: Replica reports role=master via INFO replication
Pods restart and reach Ready status

remediation_steps.description: Trigger a rolling restart of the inventory‑api deployment to ensure it reconnects to the newly promoted Redis primary.
verification: Application logs show successful Redis connection without ERR_STORAGE_EXHAUSTION_333

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Validation
remediation_steps.description: Run synthetic health checks and verify that error rates have returned to baseline.
commands: kubectl logs -l app=inventory-api -n prod --since=5m | grep ERR_STORAGE_EXHAUSTION_333 || echo 'No errors'
verification: Health endpoint returns HTTP 200 with status OK
No ERR_STORAGE_EXHAUSTION_333 strings in recent logs
Redis memory usage remains < 75% for 15 minutes

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert Redis configuration and memory limits to their pre‑change state, demote the promoted replica, and roll back inventory‑api to the previous container image if service degradation persists.

kubectl exec -n cache $(kubectl get pod -n cache -l app=redis-primary -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- redis-cli CONFIG SET stop-writes-on-replication-failure no

steps.description: Demote the promoted replica back to read‑only and restore original primary
commands: kubectl exec -n cache $(kubectl get pod -n cache -l app=redis-primary -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- redis-cli REPLICAOF <original-primary-host> <port>
kubectl exec -n cache $(kubectl get pod -n cache -l app=redis-replica -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- redis-cli REPLICAOF NO ONE
verification: INFO replication shows original primary role=master

steps.description: Revert Redis StatefulSet memory limit to original value (e.g., 2Gi)

verification: Pods are Ready and logs show no new storage exhaustion errors
